subject: PO mapping and invoice cadence for planogram SKU lanes
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novapulse.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@novapulse.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PO requirements + invoice cadence question for planogram SKU lanes

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency/cost numbers. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups before we can finalize a purchase order. Can you confirm the following so I can map this into our ERP?

- Can Redwood accept multiple PO numbers against a single contract (we need one PO per business unit / planogram)?
- Invoice cadence: our AP team prefers weekly invoices for SKU/planogram changes, but they can do monthly statements if necessary. Is weekly possible?
- Invoice format: we need the PO number to appear in the invoice header and in the invoice line matching (format: PO-<BU>-YYYY). We also require vendor tax ID and remit address on each invoice.
- Net terms: our policy defaults to net60; would Redwood consider net60 for annual committed spend, or do you require net45?

I attached our standard PO template for reference. If you can outline what we need from our side (PO formatting, any additional vendor setup metadata), I’ll pull in Tom from AP to confirm.

Appreciate it — I’m trying to keep the procurement checklist short so legal can sign quickly.

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Novapulse

Attachment: Novapulse_PO_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novapulse.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO requirements + invoice cadence question for planogram SKU lanes

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear checklist, and for sending the PO template. Good news: we can support multiple PO numbers tied to a single subscription/contract, and we have a couple of flexible invoice rails. Quick notes:

- Multiple POs: our billing system can map multiple PO numbers to one account if the PO number is included in a dedicated invoice field or in the invoice header. If your ERP requires the PO on each invoice line, we can include it in the CSV/EDI export.
- Weekly invoices: we can run weekly invoices as a pilot for the first 90 days (this is what some retail customers do to keep SKU changes aligned). After stabilization we typically convert to monthly statements to reduce AP workload.
- PO format: we can accept your PO-<BU>-YYYY convention; please confirm each BU code in advance so we can whitelist the pattern.
- Net terms: standard enterprise offering is net45, but we’re open to net60 for a 12-month committed spend with a small prepayment reserve or an early-pay discount. If Novapulse can commit to a fixed annual minimum, we can offer the net60 concession and tiered discounts.

I attached our Redwood_Billing_Guide that explains the fields we require for ERP mapping and the exact CSV/EDI headers. Two small asks: (1) please provide the exact remit address and W-9/TIN to match the vendor record; (2) if you require EDI, let us know the connector details and expected file frequency.

Next step: if Tom can confirm weekly invoice acceptance for the pilot and list BU codes, I’ll draft a short billing amendment to include in the SOW.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Billing_Guide.pdf (PDF)

Marcus — quick clarification from AP after reviewing your billing guide. Two items they flagged:

1) Our ERP requires a unique PO per BU and the PO must be present on each invoice line for automated matching — that’s non-negotiable. Can you confirm the EDI/CSV mapping will include the PO value on each line?

2) Net terms: Novapulse procurement can move to net45 for a 12-month committed spend, but we will need the following in writing: (a) a 90-day weekly invoice pilot, (b) a cap on price increases for the first 12 months, and (c) an early-pay discount structure (1% for payment within 15 days).

We’d also like to discuss a small packaging discount: if Redwood can provide a 10% discount on planogram SKU unit prices when we commit to the annual minimum, we can route the first PO this week. Tom — can you confirm the BU codes and expected weekly invoice volume (we estimate ~20 line changes/week per BU).

Thanks,
Alice

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novapulse.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO requirements + invoice cadence question for planogram SKU lanes

Hi Alice — appreciate the rapid run-through with AP. We can accommodate your asks with the following commercial and operational clarifications:

- PO on each line: confirmed. We will populate the PO value in the invoice line item CSV and EDI export. Please share the BU code list and we’ll add pattern whitelisting.
- Weekly pilot: we’ll run weekly invoices for the first 90 days (no additional billing fees). After 90 days we recommend monthly statements unless you prefer continuing weekly.
- Net terms/discounts: Redwood can offer net60 for a 12-month committed spend of $720k+ ARR tied to planogram SKUs, subject to a 10% prepayment reserve held as credit (applies only to the initial billing run). Alternatively, if you prefer no reserve, we can do net45 and provide a 10% unit discount on planogram SKUs for the first 12 months.

- Pricing caps and early-pay discount: we’ll lock price change caps for 12 months in the amendment. For early-pay you proposed 1% within 15 days — we can support that as a standard early-pay concession.

I attached a one-page amendment (Proposed_AMENDMENT_v1.docx) that captures the weekly pilot, PO mapping rules, BU whitelist, and both commercial options (net60 + reserve OR net45 + 10% discount). Please review and we can route this through DocuSign once you pick the preferred commercial path.

Next steps:
1) Novapulse to confirm BU codes and expected weekly invoice lines (Tom) — this enables whitelist and EDI mapping.
2) Choose commercial path (net60 + reserve OR net45 + SKU discount) so I can mark the amendment.
3) Sign amendment via DocuSign and we’ll kick off vendor setup and weekly invoice pilot.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the amendment.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
